title: QuickFlow ops diary — throughput experiments
content:
Experiment log (personal quicksheet) — QuickFlow Ops Diary

Notes to self:
- Triage throughput regressions when TTL change rolled out (kv-cache TTL=45s). saw drop in tokens/s under tail-load. Suspect eviction thrash on hot prefixes.
- Keep short, actionable rows: date, exp id, model, hw, batch, seq, tokens/s, p50_ms, p95_ms, est $/1k, hit_rate, notes

Table:
Date | Exp | Model | HW | Batch | Seq | Tokens/s | p50_ms | p95_ms | est $/1k | cache_hit | Notes
2024-02-05 | QF-04 | redwood/gpt-small-8b | A100-40GB | 8 | 128 | 11,200 | 32 | 78 | 0.035 | 0.62 | baseline w/ prefix cache warm
2024-02-07 | QF-05 | redwood/gpt-small-8b | A100-40GB | 16 | 128 | 18,900 | 46 | 120 | 0.028 | 0.58 | higher throughput but p95 regressed, investigate batching queue
2024-02-10 | QF-07 | redwood/gpt-small-8b q4_0 | A100-40GB | 32 | 128 | 27,400 | 71 | 160 | 0.019 | 0.55 | quantized tests — small mem wins, KV I/O slightly higher
2024-02-18 | QF-11 | redwood/gpt-small-8b | A100-40GB | 8 | 256 | 9,300 | 45 | 110 | 0.041 | 0.81 | long sequences: cache hit up but latency up due to KV inflation
2024-03-10 | QF-19 | redwood/gpt-medium-13b | A100-80GB | 4 | 128 | 6,150 | 95 | 220 | 0.12 | 0.49 | cold start penalties; prewarmed hosts helped (see notes)
2024-03-18 | QF-22 | redwood/gpt-small-8b | A100-40GB | 24 | 128 | 23,800 | 62 | 140 | 0.021 | 0.60 | tuned batching window=10ms, reduced p95 ~10%

Quick observations:
- Batching window matters a lot for p95 under variable arrival rates. 10ms seems a decent sweet spot for regional tests.
- Cache hit rate correlates with p50 but not always with p95 — when hit_rate high and p95 worse, likely eviction thrash or background transfers.
- Quantized path (q4/q8) reduces $/1k but sometimes increases p95 due to memory-bound copies. Need kernel-level profiling.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run QF-05 with per-host prefetch (ticket: JIRA-INFR-4821) to see if queue spikes decrease.
- Add perf counters for KV swap ops (ops/sec) and log alongside tokens/s.
- Check whether rollout that changed cache TTL coincides with customer-reported latency spike (lookup: slack thread above).
- Verify if A100-80GB hosts show same cache thrash pattern at high batch sizes or if larger memory masks it.

Replication snippet (local dev):
# quick curl to reproduce small-batch scenario (dev cluster)
# note: use LOCAL_API_KEY and endpoint stub
curl -s -X POST 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $LOCAL_API_KEY\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-small-8b","input":"tokenize test repeat\", "max_tokens":64, "batch_size":8}' 
  http://local-dev:8080/v1/generate | jq .

Experiment checklist before filing ticket:
- [ ] reproduce locally at similar QPS
- [ ] capture KV swap metrics (kv.swap.*) for 60s window
- [ ] snapshot host memory/free lists
- [ ] attach sample traces (p50/p95 spans) from 1 host

Quick heuristics (for next on-call):
- If p95 > 3x p50 and cache_hit > 0.6, suspect evictions: bump TTL to 2x for affected prefixes and monitor.
- If tokens/s drops while batch_size grows, check for kernel-copy stalls and GPU memory pressure.

Random personal notes (scratch):
- Tried a naive LRU tweak locally (wip) — small improvement in hit churn but not stable under synthetic fanout.
- Talk to Ravi about adding a light-weight KV inspector endpoint (read-only) for debugging live hosts.

End of sheet — will tidy and move to confluence if results hold.
